h1: The 7 Best Heated Portable Carpet Cleaners for Set-In Stains in 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Heated Spot Cleaners: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 heated portable carpet cleaners from BISSELL, Vacmaster, Armor All and Starrybot, compared on heat, tools, pets and price.
summary: The BISSELL Little Green HydroSteam is the heated spot cleaner to buy if you want the strongest active heating system in a portable body. The ProHeat Pet 3969 is the better value for pet households, the SpotClean ProHeat adds a stair tool and self-cleaning hose, and the Vacmaster is the budget way to get real heat.
intro: Heat sounds like a clear upgrade for a spot cleaner, and often it is, but only when the heat is active. Many machines simply sell a warm label while pouring in cold tap water you heated yourself. Active heating means the machine warms the solution as it cleans, which loosens oily and set-in stains that cold cleaning leaves behind. That is the feature this ranking actually sorts on.

We looked at seven heated portable machines, reading the listings for how the heat is delivered, what tools come with the machine, and who each model targets. Nothing here is lab data, and where a listing offers no figure for tank size or temperature, we say so rather than guess.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green HydroSteam Portable Carpet Cleaner, 3618
products.verdict: The most capable active heating system in a Little Green body.
products.description:
The HydroSteam sits at the top of BISSELL's heated portable line and is the machine the listing singles out for the strongest active heating system. It is built in the familiar Little Green format: a compact body, a hose and a handheld tool, with a clean-solution tank and a recovery tank.

Heat does the heavy lifting on old coffee rings, greasy food spots and dried pet accidents, where cold water barely loosens the residue. This model earns first place because it commits to heat more than any other unit here, but that comes with the highest price tier we reviewed, $200 to $500, and a heavier body than the plain models.

Buy it if your stains are stubborn and recurring and you want maximum heat. Skip it if you only wipe up fresh spills, where the cheaper units clean just as well.
products.idealFor: Homes fighting old, stubborn stains on carpet and sofas.
products.skipIf: Your messes are mostly fresh and light.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green ProHeat Pet Portable Deep Cleaner, 3969
products.verdict: Active heat plus pet-specific tools, at roughly half the cost of the HydroSteam.
products.description:
The ProHeat Pet 3969 combines active heat with tooling aimed at pet messes. It is the pet-focused member of the ProHeat family and is priced at $100 to $200, well under the HydroSteam.

Pet urine and vomit respond well to warmth, since the proteins and oils that anchor the odour loosen more easily in heated solution. It gives up the HydroSteam's top-tier heating, but for a household with a dog or cat the specialised tool matters more than a few extra degrees. It also costs far less, which is why it holds second place rather than lower.

Buy it if pets are the reason you are shopping. Skip it if you have no pets and want the strongest heat available.
products.idealFor: Dog and cat owners who want heat on pet stains.
products.skipIf: You have no pets and want maximum heat.

products.name: Bissell SpotClean ProHeat Portable Carpet Cleaner for Carpet and Upholstery
products.verdict: A stair tool and self-cleaning hose make this the most convenient heated model to maintain.
products.description:
The SpotClean ProHeat pairs heated cleaning with a stair tool and a self-cleaning hose, both of which solve day-to-day annoyances. The stair tool is shaped for tread edges and risers, and the hose rinses itself so residue and sour smells do not build up inside.

Those conveniences make it a good family machine, and it is priced at $100 to $200. It sits behind the pet-focused unit because it lacks a dedicated pet tool, which matters in homes with animals. For a household with carpeted stairs and a sofa, though, the stair tool is the feature you will use most.

Buy it if you have carpeted stairs and want a heated machine that cleans itself. Skip it if you have heavy pet messes.
cons: Same price tier as pet model
products.idealFor: Homes with carpeted stairs and family sofas.
products.skipIf: Pet accidents are your main concern.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green ProHeat Portable Deep Cleaner and Spot Cleaner, 2513E
products.verdict: Active heating at a lower price, in the classic Little Green shape.
products.description:
The 2513E is a deep cleaner and spot cleaner with active heating, positioned for buyers who want heat at a lower price. At $100 to $200 it is the base ProHeat, without the pet tools or the stair tool the premium siblings add.

The case for it is simplicity. A heated Little Green with proven design is easy to find parts for, and for a household that mostly faces coffee, wine and kid spills, the extra tools above are optional. It lands fourth because those same tools give the machines above it a wider range of jobs, and because it is the plainest of the BISSELL heated options.

Buy it if you want heat without paying for extras. Skip it if you want dedicated pet or stair tooling.
pros: Active heating at a lower price
products.idealFor: Buyers who want heated cleaning without extras.
products.skipIf: You want pet or stair tools in the box.

products.name: Vacmaster 500 Series Heated Carpet and Upholstery Spot Cleaner Machine
products.verdict: A budget-minded heated spot cleaner from a brand known for wet and dry vacuums.
products.description:
The Vacmaster 500 Series is a heated carpet and upholstery spot cleaner aimed at buyers who want active heat on a tighter budget, still within the $100 to $200 tier. Vacmaster is better known for shop vacuums, so the pitch is more workshop than living room.

Its position here reflects brand confidence rather than a known weakness. BISSELL has decades of carpet-care history, and that translates into spare parts and tool ecosystems the Vacmaster cannot yet match. The listing gives little tool detail, so you are buying the heat and the price, not a bundle.

Buy it if you want to try heated cleaning without paying BISSELL prices. Skip it if long-term parts support matters most.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers curious about heated cleaning.
products.skipIf: You want a long parts and support track record.

products.name: Starrybot Portable Carpet Cleaner with Steam, 18Kpa Spot Cleaner
products.verdict: Steam alongside heated solution, with an 18Kpa suction rating, for $50 to $100.
products.description:
The Starrybot combines steam with heated solution and lists an 18Kpa suction rating. It is the cheapest heated option here, in the $50 to $100 tier, and it targets buyers who want steam as well as hot water.

Steam is helpful for sanitising upholstery and loosening dried stains, but a steam claim does not replace a proven extraction system. The 18Kpa figure is a manufacturer rating, so treat it as marketing rather than a lab result. Compared with the BISSELL machines, you give up brand support and tool breadth for the lower price.

Buy it if you want steam and heat for the smallest outlay. Skip it if you need established service and parts.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who want steam on upholstery.
products.skipIf: You need long-term parts and support.

products.name: Armor All SCB1001H Heated Carpet and Upholstery Auto Detail Spot Cleaner
products.verdict: A heated spot cleaner built around car seats, floor mats and vehicle upholstery.
products.description:
The Armor All SCB1001H is a heated carpet and upholstery spot cleaner positioned for auto detailing. It is sold to people who want to clean car seats, floor mats and trunk liners at home, and it falls in the $100 to $200 range.

It places last only because the brief for this guide is broad household use, and the Armor All is narrower. Vehicle interiors are a great use for a heated portable machine, since seat fabric hides old drink spills and kid mess that cold cleaning leaves behind. But if your main job is a living-room rug and a family sofa, a more general machine suits you better.

Buy it if you detail cars and want a heated machine for them. Skip it if your priority is home carpet and stairs.
products.idealFor: Car owners who want to detail seats and mats.
products.skipIf: Home carpet and stairs are your main use.

whatMatters.detail: Active heat means the machine warms the cleaning solution as it works. Warmth loosens grease, dried food and pet residue, so it helps most on old stains. Check the listing for the words heated or active heat, and be wary of vague claims.

Hotter is not always better. Some synthetic carpets and delicate upholstery can be damaged by very hot water, so check the care tag on your furniture and rug. Test any heated cleaning on a hidden spot first.
A stair tool, a pet hair tool and a wide upholstery head each solve different jobs. Count what is in the box, because accessories are an extra cost later. The right tool matters as much as the heat.

Heat helps cleaning, but suction decides how dry the carpet ends up. A wet carpet takes hours to dry and can smell if it stays damp. Look at any stated suction number as a manufacturer claim, and plan for good airflow after cleaning.

Heated machines cool and sit with dirty water in the recovery tank, which can smell if you leave it. Empty and rinse both tanks after each use. A self-cleaning hose, as on the SpotClean ProHeat, makes this easier.

faq.q: Do heated spot cleaners work better than cold ones?
faq.a: On greasy, dried or protein-based stains, usually yes. Warmth loosens residue so that the brush and suction can lift it. On fresh spills the difference is smaller.
Using boiling water or harsh chemicals the maker does not recommend. Follow the instructions for water temperature and cleaning solution, since the wrong choice can damage the machine or fabric.

faq.q: Is the HydroSteam worth it over the ProHeat Pet?
faq.a: If your stains are old and stubborn, yes, because the HydroSteam has the strongest heat. For most pet households, the ProHeat Pet gives you heated cleaning with the right tooling for much less.
Add water and solution to the clean tank, connect the hose and tool, then plug the machine in. Some units need a short warm-up before the heat reaches the nozzle.

faq.q: How do I keep the machine from smelling?
faq.a: Empty the recovery tank after each use and rinse both tanks and the hose. Leave the lids off so the interior can dry fully.

faq.q: Can I use heated cleaning on any fabric?
faq.a: No. Check the care tag, avoid silk or delicate fabrics, and test a hidden area first. Some rugs and upholstery react to heat and water.

finalTake: For stubborn stains, the BISSELL Little Green HydroSteam is the best heated portable carpet cleaner here because it commits to the strongest active heat. The ProHeat Pet 3969 is the smart buy for pet homes, and the SpotClean ProHeat suits anyone with carpeted stairs. If you want to try heat on a budget, the 2513E or Vacmaster does it for less. Always test heat on a hidden patch first.
